decision: Close feat/docs-agents-memory-architecture as superseded rather than merging
why: git cherry shows only 1 genuinely-new commit (docs(plans): add remaining work PRD); its big commit e3f6bce is already upstream on github/main. The single new commit's payload is docs/plans/2026-04-16-remaining-work-prd.md at 343 lines, which codex/composition-runtime-assembly carries forward at 451 lines (+124 insertions). Merging it would regress the PRD.
Sole content is apps/docs/.astro/content-modules.mjs, an Astro generated build-cache file; the diff is pure Map-entry reordering with zero semantic change. Not source.

decision: Close codex/composition-runtime-assembly as already-merged, not via a new PR
why: git cherry showed 52 '+' commits, but that was a squash-merge artifact. Tree diff branch->github/main is 17 files/+163-45 consisting solely of CI workflow hardening, codeql.yml, and release-please CHANGELOG/version bumps - ZERO source files. All 6 key new source files (compose/runtime-types.ts, creatures/types.ts, materials/encoders.ts, props/types.ts, runtime-composition.test.ts, CompositionExamples.tsx) verified present on main. Landed on main as ebef2733 'feat: consolidate composition runtime package'.

decision: Rescue PR #21 (feat/comprehensive-tests-and-readmes) as a fresh branch instead of closing or rebasing
why: PR #21 is CONFLICTING/DIRTY against a 3800-file-divergent main, so rebasing is infeasible. But 19 test files (590 cases) target src modules that ALL still exist on main - imports verified against main's exports. Cherry-picking just the test files onto current main preserves the coverage without dragging the branch's stale src/README/lockfile changes.

decision: Delete model-synth 'passes rigged flag as is_a_t_pose' test rather than repair it
why: It stubs exactly 2 globalThis.fetch calls, but main's character({rigged:true}) now performs generate -> refine -> rigging create -> rigging poll. The mock queue is coupled to request COUNT, not behaviour. main's clients.test.ts already covers rigged:true properly via sub-API spies.

decision: Keep Tone.js mocks as `function` expressions with targeted biome-ignore comments
why: The SUT calls `new Tone.NoiseSynth()` while assertions use expect(Tone.NoiseSynth).toHaveBeenCalled(), so each mock must be BOTH a vi.fn() spy AND constructible. Arrow functions have no [[Construct]] slot; biome's useArrowFunction rule rewrites them and breaks 40 tests. A class-based wrapper satisfies `new` but breaks the spy assertions. The suppression documents a real language constraint, not a silenced warning.

@testing-library/react@16 requires dom>=10 as a peer, but the workspace resolved a transitive 9.3.4. Pinning it resolves the unmet peer and drops ~30 legacy polyfill packages (deep-equal subtree) from the lockfile.

decision: Use corepack pnpm@9.15.9 for all lockfile operations in this repo
why: CI pins PNPM_VERSION 9. Local pnpm 11 relocates pnpm.overrides out of package.json, producing ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH on CI's frozen install and rewriting ~2400 lockfile lines plus injecting placeholder allowBuilds stubs into pnpm-workspace.yaml.

decision: Fix the CodeQL high-severity alert rather than dismiss it as pre-existing
why: js/insecure-temporary-file fired on src/clients/base.ts:282, a file PR #119 does not touch. But the taint source was MY test's hardcoded '/tmp/models/model.glb' literal flowing into fs.writeFileSync. The alert is legitimately attributable to the PR even though the flagged line is in untouched src. Switched to mkdtemp() per-case temp dirs with cleanup; the happy-path case now also asserts the written bytes instead of swallowing the write error, so coverage is strictly stronger.

decision: Leave pre-existing biome noNonNullAssertion errors in audio-synth/tests/presets.test.ts unfixed
why: Those 5 errors exist on main before this PR and are in a file this PR does not otherwise touch. CI's lint script is scoped to 'biome lint src/', so tests/ findings do not gate any check (verified: npm run lint exits 0). Fixing them would expand the PR diff into unrelated files without changing any CI outcome.

decision: Do not add a packageManager pin to package.json in this PR
why: Local pnpm 11 vs CI's PNPM_VERSION 9 caused repeated lockfile churn; pinning packageManager would prevent recurrence. But it changes tooling behaviour for every contributor and every CI job, which is a separate concern from restoring test coverage. Flagged to the lead as follow-up rather than smuggled into a test PR.

decision: No code change for the 25 failing packages/core store.test.ts cases — local Node-version artifact, not a bug on main
why: Failures reproduce identically on clean github/main, so not caused by PR #119. Root cause: Node 26 defines a native Storage constructor but leaves localStorage undefined unless --localstorage-file is passed; jsdom 28 sees Storage present and declines to provision its own, so localStorage is undefined. Runtime confirmed it: 'ExperimentalWarning: localStorage is not available because --localstorage-file was not provided'. Proof: NODE_OPTIONS=--localstorage-file makes all 28 pass on Node 26. CI pins NODE_VERSION 22, which has no native Storage, so jsdom provisions normally and the suite passes there. Adding environmentOptions.jsdom.url does NOT fix it (tried and reverted) — the origin was never the problem.

decision: Ignore the failing ai-reviewer.yml workflow as a pre-existing infra issue, not a merge blocker
why: It fails on 100% of runs across every branch, including unrelated dependabot PRs (checkout-7.0.1, setup-node-7.0.0, claude-code-action-1.0.166/173/179) that predate this work. It is an auxiliary Claude-review workflow, almost certainly a missing/expired API secret, and it does not appear in the PR's check list. main has no branch protection, so there are no required status checks at all.
